title: An embryo-derived peptide signal directs endosperm polarity in Arabidopsis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC core record (isOpenAccess=N, inEPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, hasDbCrossReferences=N, hasTMAccessionNumbers=N; no accession of any kind in the indexed text). NCBI GEO searched by topic (IKU2/endosperm/polarity, PIPL7 - zero hits) and by every author with deposits (Figueiredo 6 series, Nobori 16, Creff 2, Rhodes 4, Landrein 0): I pulled the summaries of all recent ones and none matches this study. ENA study search, EBI BioStudies/ArrayExpress search, and Zenodo search on PIPL7 and 'endosperm polarity' all returned nothing for this paper. The one NCBI PMC link attached to the record resolves to an unrelated Plant Journal review (PMC13157962). The bioRxiv preprint (DOI 10.64898/2025.12.11.693621) exists but the server returned HTTP 429 (rate limited) on all four attempts at its full text and supplementary-material pages, so I could not read its data availability statement.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the biology comes from the abstract plus the authors' institutional news piece: receptor kinase HAIKU2 (IKU2) with transcription factor MINISEED3 acts through WOX8/WOX9 to set endosperm polarity, mediated by the secreted peptide PIPL7 made in the embryo. The news piece says the work used genetics, confocal bioimaging, transient receptor-ligand expression assays, and single-cell/spatial expression analysis (the latter most likely re-analysis of the authors' existing public atlases, e.g. GSE226097). No sample sizes, no measurement tables, no file list was visible to me.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. No dataset of any kind is findable for this paper. The article is subscription-only with no PubMed Central copy and no supplementary files exposed through Europe PMC; GEO, SRA, BioProject, ENA, ArrayExpress/BioStudies and Zenodo searches all came back empty; the bioRxiv preprint's full text and supplement pages returned HTTP 429 on four tries. There is nothing to download.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessable, and almost certainly fail. The quantitative content of a paper like this lives in figure-panel measurements (seed size, nuclear position, fluorescence polarity index per seed) that would have to be reconstructed from paywalled source-data files, not read from a provided column.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessable: no files. The only 'input' present in the public text is a handful of Arabidopsis gene names (IKU2, MINI3, WOX8, WOX9, PIPL7/AT4G11402).

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessable: no measurement table was reachable.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL on design even if the files appeared. The experimental unit is a genotype or a seed scored by microscopy; studies of this type report tens of genotypes and hundreds of seeds, far under the ~1,500-row bar, and I verified no row count at all.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Imaging-derived phenotype tables would be tiny; this is the only killer that is not a problem, and it is moot.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessable: nothing to count against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable. Phenotype scores would be direct microscopy measurements (good provenance in principle), but with no files I cannot trace a single label to a measurement.

integration.partner_dataset: none usable - with no data from this paper there is nothing to join
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: this paper contributes one receptor-peptide pair and no table to join on.

controls.positive_control: n/a - evaluation stopped at Part A

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper publishes a mechanism, not a dataset, and no measurement file from it is publicly downloadable.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use plant gene sequences and expression patterns to predict which small secreted peptide activates which receptor protein in seeds.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on known plant peptide-receptor pairs (sequence of the small secreted peptide plus sequence of the receptor kinase, together with where each is switched on across seed cell types). This paper contributes exactly one new pair (PIPL7 with HAIKU2), so the example count from this source is 1.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a given peptide-receptor pair is a real signalling partnership; the true answer would come from laboratory binding and activation assays, the kind of transient-expression test the authors ran to show HAIKU2 responds to PIPL7.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Plant developmental biologists have hundreds of orphan receptor kinases and hundreds of unassigned peptide genes, and each pairing currently costs months of genetics; a ranked shortlist would redirect which crosses they make. But this paper supplies one data point, not a training set.

ml_idea: No viable machine learning project from this paper. The underlying biological question - predicting which small secreted peptide binds which plant receptor kinase - is interesting, but it would have to be built from a curated collection of previously published pairs (and the public Arabidopsis single-nucleus seed atlases such as GSE226097), with this paper contributing a single additional positive example. That is a different project, resting on different data.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; the evaluation stopped at Part A1 because no data file exists to size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Search GEO, SRA, ENA, BioStudies and Zenodo for any accession attached to the paper or its authors from 2025-2026. I did this and found none, which killed it in under fifteen minutes.

verdict_reason: A1 fails outright: this is a subscription-only Science mechanism paper with no PubMed Central copy, no supplementary files reachable through Europe PMC, and no deposit in GEO, SRA, ENA, ArrayExpress/BioStudies or Zenodo under any author or topic search; the bioRxiv preprint's pages were rate-limited (HTTP 429) on four attempts. Even if the supplement were opened, it is confocal imaging and seed-phenotype scoring across a handful of genotypes, which fails A5 on row count and A2 because the quantity to predict would have to be built from figure source data.
